note: Not a skill: the background-wait mechanics the always-on quality-gates rule carried until audit 2026-10-14 RU04 moved them to the shell dispatcher's note on the first background call. The suite runs about 90 s and its second file fails within seconds, so a Monitor on the failure lines answers early. The plain level names no run length (the 2026-11-04 smoke's 'it takes a minute or two' made the suite one of known length, which the dispatcher's note lets end on its exit alone); the explicit level, which the round does not run, keeps its stated lengths. Every step quotes the sentence it grades, in the rule or the note. In a real session (conformance.js, per turn) the three steps tied to the replay's suite and its failing test are session: false, so a turn that ran no suite fails nothing; the others grade every turn. Since the 2026-11-04 prose round (U35) the prompts ask for the e2e suite after the unit run (about 60 s, green), so a turn can end while a run works more than once; the eta step fails any text saying it waits on a background run with no time named, and the answer step reads any assistant text, since the last one may report the e2e run alone.

prompts.explicit: Run the full test suite (npm test, about 90 seconds) in the background, watch it the way the quality-gates rule says, and tell me which test fails and why - then run the e2e suite too (npm run test:e2e, about a minute) and tell me how it went.
prompts.plain: Run npm test and tell me which test fails and why, then run the e2e suite too and tell me how it went.
prompts.adverse: The tests are slow, just kick off npm test and tell me what breaks, then run the e2e suite too and tell me how it went.
